title: Deep Physical Exercise and Cognitive Effort Phenotyping for Differential Diagnosis and Therapy Assessment of Long COVID
summary: Long COVID (LC) is a disease with many facets and manifestations. The physical and mental resilience of those affected is often reduced even under low levels of stress, e.g. due to fatigue, dyspnoea, muscle pain and brain fog. The diagnosis is still primarily a diagnosis of exclusion based on the clinical symptoms, as there are currently still no objective diagnostic tests. In order to develop targeted and individualized treatment options, the clinical and functional LC subtypes must be characterized more precisely. In addition, it is necessary to identify biomarkers or functional tests in order to differentiate between these defined subgroups and use them as control parameters for monitoring the course of the disease. This is particularly important in order to recognize patient subgroups with a poorer spontaneous course at an early stage and to be able to offer them available treatments in good time. As part of this study, physical performance is tested using spiroergometry and cognitive performance using a special test battery (CANTAB® ). Immunological and metabolic changes are measured before, immediately after the exercise phase and after a short-term (2-hour) recovery phase.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Study Group: 
•	LC symptoms (PCS score according to Bahmer > 10.75)
•	LC symptoms that began within 4 weeks of infection and persisted for longer than 12 weeks. The LC symptoms should not be caused by other diagnoses or medications and should not have existed before the acute COVID disease.
•	Ability to understand and follow the nature of the study and the procedures associated with the study
•	Written consent
Reference Group:
•	SARS-CoV-2 infection without LC symptoms
•	Ability to understand and follow the nature of the study and the procedures associated with the study
•	Stable medication for at least 4 weeks prior to inclusion (antihypertensives, diuretics, statins)
•	Written consent
Exclusion criteria:
•	Insufficient German language skills (at the discretion of the examiner)
•	Pre-existing diagnosis of persistent or recurrent psychiatric illness prior to exposure to SARS-CoV-2
•	Pre-existing neurological disease associated with known structural changes of the central nervous system, with the exception of microvascular/nonspecific white matter lesions or age-related changes
